Insights: From Alice’s sum = 2·Bob’s sum and after‑5‑sweet transfer both sums equal, we get B + y = 10 and A + x = 20. Hence x=20−A, y=10−B.  
Equations from products: A·x=4B·y → A(20−A)=4B(10−B); and after transfer A(x−5)=B(y+5) → A(15−A)=B(15−B).  
Search A∈[1,20], B∈[1,9] (since B+y=10) satisfying both gives unique solution A=10, B=5.  
Product of ages = 10·5 = **50**.  

Pitfalls: Mis‑interpreting “product” (must be age·sweets) and ensuring x≥5.

Insights: From “sum double” and “after 5‑sweet transfer sums equal” get B+s_B=10, A+s_A=20. So s_B=10−B, s_A=20−A. Use product condition A·s_A=4·B·s_B and transfer product A(s_A−5)=B(s_B+5). Test integer 1≤B≤10, A≤15, s_A≥5. Only solution A=10, B=5. Product ages = 50. Pitfalls: assume sums equal after transfer, not equal to original; require s_A≥5.
